metadata.title: Secure Data Platform SSPP
metadata.remarks: System Security and Privacy Plan governing the institutional Secure Data Platform, establishing authoritative governance, protection requirements, and lifecycle discipline for institutional data.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: The Secure Data Platform defines how institutional data is classified, handled, protected, retained, and disposed of so that trust in information is preserved across all applications and services.

props.name: platform-role
props.remarks: Secure Data is a Tier-1 institutional platform upon which all digital services, compliance obligations, and decision-making depend.

props.name: implements-pattern
props.remarks: This SSPP is the authoritative implementation and assurance anchor for the Trusted Data composite security pattern.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Secure Data relies on Secure Identity for attribution, access enforcement, and accountability.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Secure Data relies on Secure Network for protected transport, segmentation, and monitoring.

props.name: data-trust-model
props.remarks: All data trust, protection, and lifecycle controls are driven by declared data classification and approved purpose of use.

props.name: data-governance
props.remarks: Data ownership, classification, handling, and retention rules are defined centrally and inherited by applications.

props.name: cryptographic-trust
props.remarks: Cryptographic protections depend on managed keys, approved algorithms, and enforceable lifecycle controls.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.value: PL, AC, IA, AU, SC, SI, MP
props.remarks: Secure Data aligns with NIST SP 800-53 control families governing data protection, access enforcement, monitoring, and lifecycle management.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Data classification aligns with NIST SP 800-60 guidance for categorization of information types.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Secure Data aligns with Privacy Framework principles for purpose limitation, minimization, and lifecycle discipline.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Institutional data frequently crosses system boundaries and requires explicit trust and responsibility definition.

props.name: cryptographic-dependency
props.remarks: All encryption, signing, and cryptographic operations protecting institutional data must use keys managed by the Key Management Platform. Application-managed cryptographic keys are prohibited.

props.name: trust-establishment
props.remarks: All cryptographic trust relationships for data access, transport, or sharing must be established and validated using the institutional PKI Platform.

props.name: data-execution-environment-requirement
props.remarks: Workflows involving Data Classification Level 4 must be executed only from Dedicated Access Workstations (DAW) as defined by the Secure Endpoint Platform.

system-implementation.remarks: The Secure Data Platform composes multiple data trust concerns under a unified governance and enforcement framework.

roles.title: Data Governance Authority
roles.remarks: Defines data classification schemes, handling rules, and retention requirements.

roles.title: Data Security Operations
roles.remarks: Operates encryption, key management, DLP, and monitoring services.

roles.title: Data Architecture Authority
roles.remarks: Ensures correct inheritance and implementation of Secure Data patterns by systems.

control-implementation.remarks: Security and privacy controls for data are implemented through Secure Data patterns and inherited by applications. This SSPP documents governance scope, dependencies, and assurance only.  Cryptographic controls for data protection are enforced exclusively through the Key Management and PKI Platforms. No system may generate, store, or distribute cryptographic keys or certificates outside these platforms. Execution environment eligibility is a mandatory constraint for data protection. For Level 4 data, Secure Endpoint DAW-tier devices are required. COBO L2 and lower endpoint tiers are not eligible, regardless of user role or authorization.
